1.n: the protasis runs to 4 (ἀπὸ δʼ ἵκετο 2 is still part of it); the apodosis begins with νῆα μέν (5) (Merry on 12.2)
epic gen. -οιο; ποταμοῖο … Ὠκεανοῖο 'the river Oceanus', as Ὠκεανὸν ποταμόν 11.639

2.n: in tmesis with ἵκετο (ἀφικνέομαι 'come to, reach')
in tmesis: ἀπὸ … ἵκετο = ἀφίκετο, + acc. of the goal (κῦμα, and νῆσον 3); still part of the protasis (Merry on 12.2)
two-termination adjective, 'with wide ways'; epic gen. -οιο; 'the great and wide sea', as against the narrow Ocean-stream (Merry on 12.2)

3.n: a second goal of ἀφίκετο (2); second accent from enclitic τʼ
= τε; 'epic τε' after the relative, of what is always so

4.n: 'dancing lawns': Dawn must have a train of nymphs (Merry on 12.4); χορός the dancing ground, as 8.260

= ἀνατολαί; only here in Homer; the plural perhaps for the sun's rising at different points of the horizon with the seasons (Merry on 12.4). Here Aeaea lies at the sunrise, though Book 10 seems to put it in the far west; Merry on 12.3 takes Homer's extreme west and extreme east as almost one point

5.n: νῆα μέν opens the apodosis (Merry on 12.2); answered by ἐκ δέ (6)

5.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

5.n: aorist ἔκελσα of κέλλω 'beach, run (a ship) ashore'; in Homer only in the Odyssey; the line = 9.546

6.n: in tmesis with βῆμεν (ἐκβαίνω 'step out'); the line = 9.150, 9.547
in tmesis: ἐκ … βῆμεν = ἐξέβημεν; unaugmented root aorist
'surf, breakers', the line of breaking waves on the beach

7.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
7.n: 'having fallen asleep' (βρίζω 'be drowsy', Iliad 4.223); in Homer only here and 9.151

9.n: δὴ τότε 'then at last'; the half-line as 9.88, 10.100
imperfect as from προϊέω (= προΐην): 'sent forth'

10.n: epic infinitive of the mixed aorist οἶσε (also taken as future); infinitive of purpose with προΐειν (9) (Merry on 12.10)
in apposition to νεκρόν; his body was left unburied in Circe's house (11.51–54)

10.p: verb · pf. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

11.n: 'logs, tree trunks', for the pyre, as Iliad 23.123

11.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
11.n: 2nd aorist ἔταμον (epic τάμνω = τέμνω); the main verb is θάπτομεν (12)
= ὅθι; with θάπτομεν (12): 'we buried him where the beach ran out to its furthest point' (Merry on 12.12)
superlative of ἄκρος, predicative: 'outermost'; cp. ἀκτῇ ἔπι προὐχούσῃ 24.82 (Merry on 12.12)

12.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

13.n: 2nd aorist passive ἐκάην; singular with two subjects, νεκρός and τεύχεα; as Elpenor had asked, 11.74

14.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
14.n: epic aorist ἔχευα: 'heap up' (a mound of earth)
in tmesis with ἐρύσαντες (ἐπερύω 'drag onto'): 'having dragged up a stone pillar thereon', on the mound (Merry on 12.14)
a stone pillar set on a grave mound, as Iliad 16.457

14.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
14.n: in tmesis: ἐπὶ … ἐρύσαντες; ἐρύω 'drag', as the epithet ῥυτός of large stones, 6.267 (Merry on 12.14)

15.n: unaugmented (= ἐπήξαμεν): 'fixed'; as Elpenor asked, πῆξαί τʼ ἐπὶ τύμβῳ ἐρετμόν 11.77; cp. Aeneid 6.232 (Merry on 12.15)
superlative of ἄκρος: 'on the top of the mound'
'well-fitted, handy' (ἀραρίσκω 'fit'), of the oar as 11.121; epic ἐϋ- = εὐ-

16.n: answered by οὐδʼ ἄρα Κίρκην; the half-line as Iliad 11.706
τὰ ἕκαστα 'these things severally', as 165 (Merry on 12.16)
'were managing, carrying out'; from διέπω (root σεπ), not the δίειπε 'tell plainly' (διεῖπον) of Iliad 10.425 (Merry on 12.16)

17.n: Ionic gen. -εω, one syllable by synizesis

17.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

17.n: epic λήθω = λανθάνω, + acc. and participle: 'nor did we escape Circe's notice in coming'

18.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.
18.n: middle 'having made herself ready', as ἐντύνασαν ἓ αὐτήν Iliad 14.162 (Merry on 12.18)

19.n: joined with ἐρυθρόν, the epithet must mean 'bright, sparkling' (Merry on 12.19)

20.n: epic μέσσος = μέσος; ἐν μέσσῳ 'in the midst'

20.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

21.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

22.n: 'twice dying' (δίς + θανεῖν): they will die again; only here in Homer; cp. Aeneid 6.134 (Merry on 12.22); a scholium writes δὶς θανέες as two words (Merry's critical note on 12.22)
properly 'when', but the temporal sense is passing into a logical one, 'whereas', like Latin cum (Merry on 12.22)
= τε; 'epic τε' of what is always so

23.n: 'food' (βιβρώσκω 'eat'); in Homer only in the Odyssey

24.n: ἅμα ἠοῖ φαινομένηφι 'when dawn appears', as Iliad 9.618

24.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. sg. fem.
24.n: epic -φι ending, here dative: 'with dawn appearing'

25.n: = πλεύσεσθε; future middle πλεύσομαι of πλέω

26.n: adverbial: μή τι 'lest in any way'
'evil contriving' (κακός + ῥάπτω 'stitch, contrive'), as κακορραφίης ἀλεγεινῆς Iliad 15.16; the plural 2.236, and cp. κακὰ ῥάπτομεν 3.118 (Merry on 12.26); causal dative

27.n: best taken as a local genitive, 'on sea', rather than with ἐπί serving both nouns, as Nitzsch has it (Merry on 12.27)
aorist subjunctive with the short vowel (= ἀλγήσητε) (Merry on 12.27)

27.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

29.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
29.n: root aorist κατέδυν: 'until the setting of the sun'

30.n: imperfect, the same in form as the present; the line = 9.162, 10.184, 10.468, 10.477

30.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

32.n: the companions, as against ἡ δʼ ἐμέ (33)
unaugmented (= ἐκοιμήσαντο); the half-line after Iliad 1.476
mooring cables from stern to shore

33.n: with both ἑλοῦσα and εἷσε (34); they were not in Circe's house, for she goes back there at 143: perhaps in some grotto or bower (Merry on 12.33)
genitive of the part taken hold of

33.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

34.n: causative aorist εἷσα 'made sit'; second accent from enclitic τε

athematic aorist middle (root λεχ- 'lie', as λέκτο 4.453); 'reclined at my feet' rather than 'lay by me', for no bed is mentioned and lying would not suit εἷσε; the scholia's προσεῖπε 'addressed' is untenable (Merry on 12.34); only here in Homer
unaugmented; epic ἐρεείνω 'ask', with ἐξ- 'question closely'

35.n: κατὰ μοῖραν 'fittingly, rightly'; the half-line as 10.16

36.n: 'mistress, lady', a title of goddesses, as 10.394, 10.549

37.n: all that happened on the voyage to Hades (Merry on 12.37)

37.g: have been brought to an end
37.n: perfect passive of πειραίνω 'bring to an end' (πεῖραρ 'end'); plural verb with a neuter plural subject

38.n: 'how, as': introduces what she will say; accent from enclitic τοι
active future 'remind', + acc. of the person
no particular god, neither Poseidon nor Helios, as the scholia suggest: 'some kindly power'; cp. ἄλλα δὲ καὶ δαίμων ὑποθήσεται 3.27 (Merry on 12.38)

39.n: accusative of the goal; the name is of doubtful origin: 'enchainers' (σειρά 'cord'), or akin to Σείριος, or 'sweet-sounding' (Merry on 12.39). In Homer they are two (the dual Σειρήνοιιν 52, 167) and live on one island
uncontracted -εαι (= ἀφίξῃ); + acc. of the goal
'epic τε' after the relative, of what they always do

40.p: indef. rel. pron. · nom. sg. masc.
40.n: epic ὅτις = ὅστις; singular after plural ἀνθρώπους; the manuscripts vary between ὅτε σφέας, ὅτι σφέας, ὅ τις σφέας and ὅς τις (Merry's critical note on 12.40)
'arrive at, reach', + acc.; subjunctive without κε in a general relative clause

41.n: 'ignorance' (ἀ- + ἰδρείη 'knowledge'); the singular only here, the plural 10.231, 10.257, 11.272
intransitive 'come near'; subjunctive without κε in a general relative clause

42.n: τῷ δέ is the apodosis to ὅς τις (41) (Merry on 12.42)
with γυνή the subject of γάνυνται (43); παρίσταται is singular with the wife alone (Merry on 12.42)

43.p: verb · aor. part. act. dat. sg. masc.

43.n: intransitive middle 'stand by', + dat.; singular with the wife alone (Merry on 12.42)
'rejoice, be glad'; Kayser would read παρίσταντʼ (Merry on 12.42)

44.n: 'clear, shrill'; cp. Alcman's λίγεια Σειρήν (Merry on 12.44)

45.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. fem.

45.n: epic -φι(ν) ending, generally taken here as a genitive with θίς, though Homer has no other -φι form depending on a noun (ἀπʼ ὀστεόφιν 14.134 has a preposition); Monro takes it as instrumental of material; or join ἀνδρῶν πυθομένων ἀμφʼ ὀστεόφιν, 'rotting round their bones', as ἀμφʼ ὀστεόφι 16.145 (Merry on 12.45)
'heap'; elsewhere in Homer θίς is the sandy shore (θῖνα, θινί); the nominative only here

46.p: verb · pres. part. mid. gen. pl. masc.

46.n: flesh and skin together, as ῥινὸν ἀπʼ ὀστεόφιν 14.134 (Merry on 12.45)

47.n: epic ἐλάαν (= ἐλᾶν, from ἐλάω = ἐλαύνω), of rowing a ship; infinitive with imperatival force, like ἀλεῖψαι (Merry on 12.47); printed here as one word (Merry prints παρὲξ ἐλάαν, as the text has it at 55, 109); the compound again Iliad 23.344
adverbial, 'on' (the ears), as ἐπʼ οὔατα (177); or in tmesis with ἀλεῖψαι (ἐπαλείφω, the compound of Alcman's allusion: Merry on 12.47)
infinitive with imperatival force (Merry on 12.47); Alcman's Κίρκη ἐπαλείψασα refers to this scene, the earliest extant allusion to a scene of the Odyssey (Nitzsch, in Merry on 12.47)

48.n: 'beeswax'; in Homer only in this book

48.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

48.n: μή τις + subjunctive 'so that no one'

49.n: epic inf. -έμεν; with ἐθέλῃσθα, as though the order were αἴ κʼ ἐθέλῃσθα ἀκουέμεν, so that the apodosis begins at δησάντων (50); Ameis instead takes ἀκουέμεν as imperatival and αἴ κʼ ἐθέλῃσθα as parenthetic (Merry on 12.47, and his critical note on 12.49)
epic αἰ = εἰ; accent from enclitic κʼ

50.n: 'bind'; 'let them bind thee hand and foot standing upright in the mast-step' (Merry on 12.50)
accusative of the part, with σε; second accent from enclitic τε

51.n: predicative, with σε (50): standing upright; the line again 162, and 179 with ἀνῆπτον
'mast-step' (ἱστός + πέδη), in which the mast is stepped; virtually the same as the μεσόδμη 'mast-box' of 2.424 (Merry, Appendix I §12); in Homer only here and 162, 179
with αὐτοῦ; with ἀνήφθω ἐκ cp. πέτρης ἐκ πείσματα δήσας 10.96 (Merry on 12.51)
the mast (ἱστοῦ), understood from ἱστοπέδῃ (Merry on 12.50)
= πείρατα, subject of ἀνήφθω: the free ends of the cords that bind him, made fast to the mast; πεῖραρ 'end', here exactly the 'rope-ends' (Merry on 12.51)
perfect passive imperative of ἀνάπτω 'fasten to'; singular verb with a neuter plural subject

52.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

52.n: epic gen. dual -οιιν: in Homer the Sirens are two (Merry on 12.39); again 167

53.n: accent from enclitic κε; 53–54 were athetized by Aristophanes, as there was no need to bind again a man once bound (Merry's critical note on 12.53)

54.n: οἱ δέ, the apodosis to εἰ δέ κε (53) (Merry on 12.54)
δέ of the apodosis; accent from enclitic σʼ
from the reduplicated by-form δίδημι (impf. δίδη Iliad 11.105): Aristarchus' reading; the manuscripts have δεόντων (Merry on 12.54 and his critical note)

55.n: 55–58: after the Sirens Odysseus has a choice of two courses, by the Wanderers (59–72) or between Scylla and Charybdis (73–110), and Circe will not choose for him (Merry on 12.55)
the Sirens; object of παρὲξ ἐλάσωσιν; accent from enclitic γε
in tmesis with ἐλάσωσιν (παρεξελαύνω 'row past'), as παρεξελάαν 47
in tmesis: παρὲξ … ἐλάσωσιν; ἐλαύνω of rowing a ship

57.p: indef. rel. pron. · nom. sg. fem.
57.n: epic -ππ- (= ὁποτέρη); indirect question, with ὁδός
epic τοι = σοι; dative of possession

58.n: infinitive with imperatival force: 'consider it for yourself' (Merry on 12.55)
'on both sides': here = ἀμφοτέρας τὰς ὁδούς, divided into ἔνθεν μὲν γάρ (59) and οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι (73) (Merry on 12.55)

59.n: 'on the one side', answered by οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι (73) (Merry on 12.55, 12.73)
two-termination adjective, uncontracted -έες: 'overhanging, beetling', as 10.131; εἰσί understood

60.n: contracted: 'roar, dash', of surf, as ῥόχθει 5.402
the sea personified, as 3.91; only in the Odyssey

61.n: predicate accusative with καλέουσι: the 'wandering' rocks (πλαγκτός, πλάζω), as Merry takes it, perhaps a sailors' tale of floating icebergs or of volcanic islets; most modern editors prefer 'striking' (πλήσσω), of rocks dashing together or of the waves dashing on them, and the ancients were divided; later identified with the Symplegades (Merry on 12.61); again 23.327
'surely, you know'; or the ethical dative of σύ
the rocks; accent from enclitic γε
a name given by the gods, as μῶλυ 10.305; the words suggest that the name had lost its meaning, or the story was half forgotten (Merry on 12.61)

62.n: 'there, by that way'; τῇ δʼ (66) is no antithesis to it, only a continuation (Merry on 12.55)
= τε; 'epic τε' of what always happens
'flying things, birds' (ποτάομαι 'fly'); only here in Homer; neuter plural with a singular verb
'go past'; the doves run their danger in passing by, and nothing is said of the rocks closing on them (Merry on 12.63)
the doves that carry ambrosia to Zeus: perhaps an allusion to the Pleiads, of whose seven stars only six are commonly seen (Merry on 12.62)

63.n: epithet of doves, as Iliad 5.778, 22.140; from τρέω 'flee in fear': the timidity shown in quick flight (Merry on 12.63)
epic ταί = αἵ, the article as relative; accent from enclitic τʼ
= τε; 'epic τε' after the relative, of what they always do

64.n: partitive: one of them (τινά understood) (Merry on 12.62)
middle 'take away (for oneself)': 'steals away one' (Merry on 12.62)
'smooth, sheer', as λισσὴ … πέτρη 3.293, 5.412, 10.4; not λίς 'lion' (Iliad 11.239); in Homer only here and 79

65.n: 'counted in': predicative with εἶναι, 'to make up the tale' (Merry on 12.62); two-termination adjective; elsewhere in Homer only Iliad 2.202

66.n: 'there, by that way', continuing τῇ μέν (62) (Merry on 12.55)
οὔ πω 'never yet'; accent from enclitic τις
νηῦς … ἀνδρῶν, set against ποτητά (62) (Merry on 12.66)
unaugmented (= ἔφυγε); a general fact, parallel to παρέρχεται (62), as the mood of ἵκηται and the tense of φορέουσι (68) show (Merry on 12.66)
subjunctive without κε in a general relative clause

67.n: = τε (τ → θ before rough breathing); 'epic τε' of what always happens
'boards, timbers' of wrecked ships; second accent from enclitic τε

68.n: 'sweep away': properly with κύματα, by a slight zeugma with θύελλαι; cp. ἀνηρείψαντο θύελλαι 4.727 (Merry on 12.68)
'storms of fire': the surf and the fire-storms destroy the ships, as if the Planctae were volcanic islets like Stromboli (Merry on 12.61)

69.n: epic κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος; La Roche reads κείνῃ 'that way', to match τῇ (62, 66) (Merry's critical note on 12.69)
root aorist (ἔπλων) of πλώω, the epic by-form of πλέω: 'sailed past'; only here in Homer

70.n: Jason's ship, here on her way home from Colchis; Merry thinks 69–72 probably a later addition (Merry on 12.70); only here in Homer

70.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
70.n: 'a care to all', i.e. famous; cp. 9.20, 'am in the thoughts of men' (Merry on 12.70); Aristarchus is said to have written πασιμέλουσα as one word (Merry's critical note on 12.70)
epic gen. -αο; Circe's brother (10.137), king of Colchis

70.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

71.n: with the aorist indicative: what would have happened
unaugmented (= ἔβαλε); the subject is probably κύματʼ ἁλός (68), and nothing is said of the rocks closing on the ship (Merry on 12.71)

72.n: 'brought her safely past'; only here in Homer

73.n: οἱ δέ, the antithesis to ἔνθεν μέν (59): 'Now, on the other side' (Merry on 12.73)
epic δύω = δύο, here with a plural noun
'the one of them', answered by τὸν δʼ ἕτερον (101) (Merry on 12.73)

74.n: perfect: 'has settled about', as κυάνεον Τρώων νέφος ἀμφιβέβηκε Iliad 16.66; νεφέλη … κυανέη runs over into 75, as Iliad 20.417–418

75.n: a vague neuter, referring to the whole of νεφέλη δέ μιν ἀμφιβέβηκε: 'this never ceases', Aristarchus' view (Merry on 12.75)
'streams away, withdraws', and so 'ceases': 'the cloud-covering never streams off it' (Merry on 12.75, after Buttmann)

76.n: the season of ripening fruit, as Iliad 22.27, 11.192

77.n: apocope: ἀμ- = ἀνα- before β; 'go up, climb'
'set foot on the top', a further stage than ἀμβαίη: Aristarchus' reading, which makes the rock wholly inaccessible; the vulgate had οὐ καταβαίη (Merry on 12.77 and his critical note)

78.n: dative of possession with εἶεν: 'he had'

79.n: 'polished all round' (περί + ξέω 'smooth'), sc. πέτρῃ; only here in Homer

79.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

80.n: epic μέσσος = μέσος: 'in the middle of the crag'

81.n: the west: πρὸς ζόφον gives the direction the cave's mouth faces, while εἰς Ἔρεβος τετραμμένον shows that it runs downward, not level into the cliff (Merry on 12.81)

81.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. neut.

81.n: with the subjunctive ἰθύνετε (82): 'just where you will steer your hollow ship past' (Merry on 12.81)

82.n: short-vowel subjunctive (= ἰθύνητε) with ἄν (81) (Merry on 12.81)

83.n: epic αἰζήϊος = αἰζηός 'vigorous, in his prime', with ἀνήρ, as Iliad 17.520; the cave's mouth is so high that the strongest bowman could not reach it (Merry on 12.83)

84.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

85.n: properly 'the render, tearer'; the link with σκύλαξ 'puppy' (86) is probably later, and may account for 86–88 and the dogs of later poets; the ancients placed her on the Italian side of the strait of Messina (Merry on 12.85)

85.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
85.n: perfect of λάσκω 'shriek, yelp' with present sense (masc. λεληκώς Iliad 22.141)

86.n: 86–88 were athetized in antiquity: how could the monster have a puppy's voice? (Merry's critical note on 12.86)
the volume of the cry is no greater than a puppy's yelp: an intentionally grotesque contrast with her size (Merry on 12.86)
'newborn', = νεογνός (Eustathius and the Etymologicum Magnum); others connect it with γάλα 'milk'; variants νεογιλλῆς, νεογηλῆς (Merry on 12.86); only here in Homer

87.n: πέλωρ, indeclinable by-form of πέλωρον 'monster', as 9.428
with the optative: potential; accent from enclitic τις

88.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

88.n: the poet takes the divine as the limit of exaggeration, as the scholia observe (Merry on 12.88)

89.n: genitive of possession with εἰσί: 'she has'

disputed: 'ugly', 'imperfect' (Ameis), 'feeble' (the scholia, Eustathius), 'pendulous' (αἰωρέω; a scholium, Curtius) or 'fore-feet' (Nitzsch); Aristarchus 'without limbs, like tentacles', Crates 'hard to guard against'; Merry thinks 'imperfect' and 'pendulous' the likeliest (Merry on 12.89); only here in Homer

91.n: 'in three rows' (τρίς + στοῖχος 'row'); only here in Homer (the adverb τριστοιχί Iliad 10.473)

93.n: answered by ἔξω δʼ (94); accent from enclitic τε
κατὰ σπείους 'in the cave', as 9.330 (Merry on 12.93)
perfect with present sense: 'has sunk into, is sunk'

94.n: 'hold out' (ἐκ + ἴσχω); only here in Homer
Ionic for βάραθρον (a variant here) 'pit, chasm', as Iliad 8.14; from the root of βορά, βιβρώσκω 'devour' (Merry on 12.94)

95.n: epic diectasis (= ἰχθυᾷ): 'fish'; elsewhere in Homer only 4.368

95.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
95.n: epic diectasis (= περιμαιμῶσα): 'searching eagerly round', + acc.; join with εἴ ποθι (96): 'questing round the rock if anywhere she may catch' (Merry on 12.95); only here in Homer

96.n: 'sea-dogs', according to Polybius (in Strabo) a kind of swordfish (Merry on 12.96)
εἰ + subjunctive without κε; accent from enclitic ποθι

97.n: a plural relative after the singular κῆτος (Merry on 12.97)
'loud-moaning' (ἀγα- + στένω 'moan'), of the roaring sea; only here in Homer

98.n: Scylla; or adverbial 'that way'; Aristophanes read τήν (Merry's critical note on 12.98)
οὔ πω ποτε 'never yet'; accent from enclitic ποτε
'unharmed' (κήρ 'doom'), as 23.328; but 'lifeless, heartless' (κῆρ 'heart') at Iliad 7.100, 11.392, 13.224 (Merry on 12.98)

99.n: apocope: παρ- = παρα-; epic 2nd aorist inf. -έειν: 'escape past'; only here in Homer

100.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

101.n: τὸν δʼ ἕτερον, in contrast to ὁ μέν (73) (Merry on 12.101)

102.n: with ἀλλήλων, εἰσί understood: 'they are near each other', as πλησίον ἀλλήλων 14.14; some wrote πλησίοι, which Düntzer adopts (Merry on 12.102 and his critical note)
'shoot an arrow across' the gap between them, which this measures (Merry on 12.102); elsewhere in Homer of shooting through the axes, 19.578, 21.76

103.n: dative of respect with τεθηλώς: 'luxuriant with leaves'

103.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
103.n: perfect of θάλλω with present sense: 'flourishing'

104.n: 'brilliant, divine'; the epithet perhaps gave rise to the later legend that she was Poseidon's daughter (Merry on 12.104)

348.n: middle 'be angered', + gen. of the cause; second accent from enclitic τι
'with upright horns', shortened from ὀρθοκεραιράων; it does not clash with ἕλικες (355) unless that means 'with crumpled horns' (Merry on 12.348); epic gen. pl. -άων

349.n: in tmesis: ἐπὶ … ἕσπωνται; subjunctive of the syncopated aorist ἑσπόμην (present ἕπομαι): 'and the rest of the gods should follow his lead' (Merry on 12.349)

350.n: = βούλομαι; 'I prefer', with ἤ (351) 'rather than', as 3.232–234 (Merry on 12.350)
'once, once for all'; in Homer only here and 22

350.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
350.n: 2nd aorist ἔχανον 'gape': πρὸς κῦμα χανών 'with one gasp open-mouthed at the wave', of drowning, as ἐπεὶ πίεν ἁλμυρὸν ὕδωρ 4.511 (Merry on 12.350)
in tmesis: ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσαι = ἀπολέσσαι; epic -σσ-

351.n: from a stem στραγγ-, as in στράγξ 'a drop': 'to be drained of strength', squeezed out drop by drop; the Harleian scholia record a variant στρέγγεσθαι (Merry on 12.351 and his critical note); in Homer only here and Iliad 15.512 (the same half-line)

351.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

352.n: in tmesis: ἐπὶ … ᾔνεον = ἐπῄνεον; uncontracted (Attic ᾔνουν)

353.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
353.n: the participle does not stand for a finite verb: after the parenthesis οὐ γὰρ … εὐρυμέτωποι (354–355) the sentence goes on with τὰς δὲ περίστησαν (356) (Nitzsch, in Merry on 12.353); the half-line = 343

355.n: = βοσκέσκοντο, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ἕλικες; iter. (-σκ-), unaugmented; middle 'graze'; the form only here in Homer
'twisted', of the horns (some take it of the rolling gait); see on ὀρθοκραιράων (348)
'broad-fronted' (εὐρύς + μέτωπον); two-termination adjective; καλαὶ βόες εὐρυμέτωποι as 262

356.n: the cows of 353, after the parenthesis (Merry on 12.353)

unaugmented intransitive root aorist (= περιέστησαν), + acc.; second accent from enclitic τε; the manuscripts have περιστήσαντο, here and at Iliad 2.410, but Bekker's conjecture περίστησάν τε is adopted in both places by all modern editors (Merry's critical note on 12.356); with no barley at hand they use oak leaves in its place (357–358); for the barley in the rite see 3.441–447 (Merry on 12.356)

357.n: oak leaves in place of the barley grains (οὐλοχύται) of the sacrifice (Merry on 12.356)

357.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
357.n: 'pluck, strip' (middle: for themselves); only here in Homer
'with lofty foliage' (ὕψι + κόμη); two-termination; epic gen. -οιο

358.n: epic short form of κριθή 'barley': the grains thrown at a sacrifice (οὐλοχύται, Iliad 2.410)

360.n: sacrificial term: thigh-bones cut out for the god; the line = Iliad 1.460, 2.423
Ionic -ῃ; here the fat, not the savor

361.n: the line = 3.458, Iliad 1.461, 2.424: the fat folded double around the thigh-bones

361.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

361.n: sacrificial term: raw bits placed on the thighs

362.n: infinitive of purpose: 'to pour (as a drink-offering)', as the old man pours wine over the burning thighs, 3.459–460, Iliad 1.462–463

362.p: verb · pres. part. mid./pass. dat. pl. neut.

363.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

363.n: contracted imperfect (= ἐπώπταον) of ἐποπτάω 'roast over (the fire)'; only here in Homer

364.n: = μῆρα, the thigh-bones of 360; neuter plural with singular verb
2nd aorist passive ἐκάην of καίω; in tmesis: κατὰ … ἐκάη
sacrificial term: heart, liver, lungs, kidneys

365.n: unaugmented (= ἐμίστυλλον); second accent from enclitic τʼ
= ἀμφί; tmesis with ἔπειραν (ἀμφιπείρω), or prep. + dat.

366.n: dative of the person affected: 'from my eyelids'
epic athematic aorist with -σσ-: 'rushed out', + gen., as Iliad 7.1
prob. from ἥδυμος 'sweet', misdivided in ἔχεν ἥδυμος

367.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔβην); βῆν … ἰέναι 'I set off'; the line = 10.407

368.n: epic ἦα (= ἦν) 'I was', not ᾖα 'I went'

368.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

368.n: epithet of ships: 'curved at both ends' (or 'rowed on both sides')

369.n: καὶ τότε 'then', the main clause after ὅτε δή (368)
Ionic κνίση = κνῖσα: the savor of burnt fat, as Iliad 1.66
epic aorist ἀμφήλυθον: here of a scent floating round the nostrils, at 6.122 of a sound round the ears (Merry on 12.369); in Homer only here and 6.122

masculine form with the feminine ἀυτμή, as θῆλυς ἀυτή 6.122, πουλὺν ἐφʼ ὑγρήν Iliad 10.27; Kayser supposed that Aristarchus read θερμὸς ἀυτμή here, but La Roche dissents (Merry's critical note on 12.369)
'breath, blast', here a smell, as of fragrance at Iliad 14.174

370.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

370.n: = μέγα, adverbial 'loudly', with γεγώνευν: Bekker's conjecture, after μέγα δʼ εὔξατο 17.239; Merry prints μετʼ ἀθανάτοισι 'among the immortals', a standing formula not to be pressed, since Odysseus was not in the gods' presence (Merry on 12.370 and his critical note)
imperfect as from γεγωνέω, unaugmented, Ionic -ευν (= -ουν): 'called so as to be heard', + dat.; first person here, third plural at 9.47

371.p: verb · pres. part. act. voc. pl. masc.
371.n: epic ἐόντες = ὄντες; μάκαρες θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες as Iliad 24.99

372.n: of the result, 'to my ruin', as εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν Iliad 9.102; later Greek would use ἐπί (Merry on 12.372)
'blind folly, ruin', the Iliad's key word
uncontracted dat. -έι; 'pitiless' (νη- + ἔλεος); νηλέι ὕπνῳ seems to leave a hiatus, but ὕπνος once began with σ (Latin somnus, sopor) (Merry on 12.372)

373.n: μέγα ἔργον 'a great deed', as 11.272 (Merry on 12.373 refers to his note there)

373.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

374.n: epic fem. ὠκέα (Attic ὠκεῖα), predicative: 'swift(ly)'; many copies have ὠκύς (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 12.374); 374–390 bear the obelus in the manuscript M and were probably rejected by Aristarchus: the scholia object that the Sun, who sees all things (323, Iliad 3.277), should have known it of himself (Merry's critical note on 12.374)

375.n: the nymph who herds the Sun's cattle with Phaethusa (132); in apposition to ἄγγελος (374)
two-termination adjective: -ος used as feminine; 'with trailing robe', as of Helen, Iliad 3.228
neuter relative ὅ used as ὅτι 'that', giving the message
dative of the person concerned: 'killed his cattle'
1st plural of the root aorist ἔκταν (κτείνω), unlike ἔκταμεν = ἐξέταμε at 9.320 (Merry on 12.375)
ἔκταμεν ἡμεῖς is Aristarchus' reading; the manuscripts give ἔκταν ἑταῖροι, from a wish to clear Odysseus of the blame (Merry's critical note on 12.375)

376.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; used as a noun

376.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

377.p: verb · pres. part. act. voc. pl. masc.

378.n: middle 'make pay, punish'; singular after the address to Zeus and the other gods (377)

379.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν) (= αἷς); dative with χαίρεσκον (380)

380.n: iter. (-σκ-), unaugmented: 'I used to be glad', + dat. ᾗσιν (379)

380.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

381.n: = ὁπότε, with the optative of repeated action in the past
οὐρανός 'sky' with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word
thematic aorist ἐτραπόμην: 'turn forward', of the sun moving on from the height of the sky toward the earth; the line after 11.18, there with ἂν and the subjunctive

382.n: with the future indicative, in a threat
οὐ (not μή) after εἰ: οὐ τίσουσι is one idea, 'refuse to pay', as οὔ φησι (Merry on 12.382)

383.n: with the genitive Ἀίδαο: 'into (the house) of Hades'

epic by-form of φαίνω, intransitive 'shine'; a scholion calls it a present for the future, and it may be a vivid present indicative, but Homeric usage points to a subjunctive after the future δύσομαι, of what the speaker resolves to do (Merry on 12.383, citing Monro)

384.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

385.n: present imperative: 'go on shining'; φαείνω in Homer only in the Odyssey (3.2, 18.308, 343)

387.n: with νῆα, 'their ship', put first for emphasis
answers μέν (385); accent from enclitic κʼ

388.n: neuter plural as adverb, 'into small pieces': join τυτθά with κεάσαιμι and βαλών with κεραυνῷ (Merry on 12.388); Zenodotus read τριχθά 'in three' (Merry's critical note on 12.388)

388.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

389.n: + gen. of the person heard from; 389–390 answer the question how Odysseus could know what passed between the Sun and Zeus, as Eustathius says; Merry finds the explanation suspicious, too punctilious a criticism for the period (Merry on 12.389)
genitive of the source with ἤκουσα

390.n: epic gen. -αο; genitive of the source with ἀκοῦσαι; a scholion on 5.79 calls Odysseus' words here a falsehood; in Merry's view the falsehood is rather Calypso's (Merry's critical note on 12.389–390)
epithet of Hermes, 'guide' or 'messenger'; meaning uncertain
infinitive of indirect statement after ἔφη

392.n: ἄλλοθεν ἄλλον 'one after another, from every side'
'walking up to each one in turn and standing by him', as 13.54: like παρασταδόν (207), but with the approach included, which suits ἄλλοθεν (Merry on 12.392)
rare: 'means, remedy' (cf. μηχανή); οὐδέ τι μῆχος as Iliad 2.342, 9.249

393.n: = δέ: it gives the reason why no remedy was possible (Merry on 12.393)

syncopated pluperfect, unaugmented (= ἀπετεθνήκεσαν): so most manuscripts, the vulgate ἀπετέθνασαν; La Roche cites forms such as ἀμφιβεβήκει to show that the augment is unnecessary (Merry's critical note on 12.393)

394.n: uncontracted plural (= τέρατα), as τεράεσσι Iliad 6.183; 'portents'

395.n: imperfect, augmented εἷρπ- as εἷλκον from ἕλκω: 'crawled on the ground' (Merry on 12.395)
the hides flayed from the cows (359)
subject of μεμύκει: neuter plural with singular verb

pluperfect of μέμυκα with imperfect sense, unaugmented: 'bellowed'; Merry on 12.395 compares Euripides, Trojan Women 439–440, of the Sun's cows, and the dried fish that leapt on the fire in Herodotus 9.120

396.n: postpositive ὡς 'as, like', accented after its noun: βοῶν ὥς 'as of cattle'

397.n: ἕξ + ἦμαρ, as ἐννῆμαρ (447); the line again 14.249
nom. pl. of ἐμός, not the dative of ἐγώ; with ἑταῖροι, as 199 and 9.555
plural as if from a 3rd-decl. ἐρίηρ; out of place here as a special epithet, a mere epic formula, and not to be taken as ironical (Merry on 12.397)

398.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
398.n: the half-line = 343, 353; the scholia record a variant ἐλόωντες (Merry's critical note on 12.398)

399.n: δὴ ἕβδομον with synizesis, as δὴ αὖτε 10.281 and δὴ ἄγρην 330 (Merry on 12.399)
in tmesis with θῆκε (ἐπιτίθημι): 'added the seventh to the tale of six' (Merry on 12.399)
in tmesis: ἐπὶ … θῆκε = ἐπέθηκε; unaugmented

400.n: καὶ τότʼ ἔπειτʼ 'then', in the apodosis, as 5.391
middle 'cease', with the participle θύων: 'ceased raging' (Merry on 12.439 compares κρίνων 440); the half-line again 426

400.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

401.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

401.n: κ-aorist of ἐνίημι 'send into', + dat.: 'put out (the ship) into'; not quite 'launch', since for a short stay the ship was moored afloat, not drawn up on shore (Merry on 12.293, to which his note on 401 refers)

402.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

402.n: in tmesis with ἐρύσαντες (ἀνερύω 'haul up'); acute before enclitic θʼ
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing

402.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
402.n: in tmesis: ἀνά … ἐρύσαντες 'having hauled up'

403.n: = ἀλλά; 403–406 again 14.301–304, there with Κρήτην μέν for τὴν νῆσον

404.n: epic gen. pl. -άων, partitive with τις ἄλλη (403); an unusual plural, also 8.284, 14.302, perhaps a plural of a general idea, as ἱπποσύναι Iliad 16.776 (Krüger, in Merry on 12.404)

405.n: δὴ τότε 'then', the main clause after ὅτε δή (403)

406.n: anastrophe: follows νηός, accent thrown back
'grow dark' (ἀχλύς 'mist'); in Homer only here and 14.304

407.n: contracted imperfect (= ἔθεε): 'ran', of a ship under way
of time: πολλὸν ἐπὶ χρόνον, here and 15.494; 'the ship ran on for no long time' (Merry on 12.407)

408.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

409.n: two ropes from the masthead, made fast one at each side of the bows; with the backstay (ἐπίτονος, 423) they took the strain of the mast, and only because both broke at once did it fall aft (Merry on 12.409)
= ἔρρηξε; ρ doubled after the augment

410.n: emphatic by its place at the head of the verse (Merry on 12.409)
all the cordage of the mast and yard, which tumbled into the hold when the mast fell aft (Merry on 12.410)

411.n: 'bilge-water', and the hold where it gathers; in Homer only here and 15.479
= κατέχυντο, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὁ; athematic aorist middle (ἐχύμην) of χέω, passive in sense; plural with the neuter plural ὅπλα
the adjective πρυμνός 'hindmost' (accent -ῇ), not the noun πρύμνη: νηὶ … πρυμνῇ 'in the stern of the ship'

412.n: epic gen. -εω (= -ου); the helmsman is not named
in tmesis: σὺν … ἄραξε = συνήραξε 'smashed together'; unaugmented

413.n: 'diver, tumbler'; dative with ἐοικώς; the ancients referred it to ἄρνες, as if 'skipping like a ram'; Curtius connects it with a word for water (Latin urinator 'diver'); for the diver's plunge cf. Iliad 16.745–748 (Merry on 12.413)

413.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

414.n: = κάππεσε; apocope: κάππεσε = κατέπεσε; the line after Iliad 12.386, 16.743
epic -φι(ν) ending, here as genitive with ἀπό: the half-deck at the stern, where the helmsman stood

415.n: 'along with' the wind and rain, or correlative with καί: 'in the same moment that he thundered, he smote the ship' (Merry on 12.415)

416.n: aorist passive of ἐλελίζω: 'shook, quivered', as Iliad 22.448 (τῆς δʼ ἐλελίχθη γυῖα)

416.p: verb · aor. part. pass. nom. sg. fem.

417.n: adverbial 'within'; or in tmesis with πλῆτο
epic θέειον = θεῖον 'sulfur', smelt where lightning strikes, as Iliad 8.135, 14.415; elsewhere in Homer used for cleansing and fumigation (Iliad 16.228; Odyssey 22.481, 493; 23.50) (Merry on 12.417)
athematic aorist middle (ἐπλήμην), unaugmented: 'was filled', + gen.

418.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); the sea-crows (εἰνάλιαι κορῶναι) of 5.66–67 (Merry on 12.418 refers to his note on 5.66)

419.n: unaugmented; passive 'be borne about in', + dat.; in Homer only here and 14.309
epic ἀποαίνυμαι (= ἀπαίνυμαι), unaugmented; the hiatus is kept by an old digamma (ἀποϝαίνυτο), as 14.309, Iliad 13.262, beside ἀπαινύμενον Iliad 11.582 (Merry on 12.419)

420.n: contracted (-αον > -ων): 'I kept pacing the length of the ship' (Merry on 12.420)

421.n: 'wash of the waves' (κλύζω 'dash'); only here in Homer
the keel, left bare, 'the sides of the ship having been torn away from it' (Merry, Appendix I on the Homeric ship, §2)

422.n: the ship's: dative of the thing concerned
in tmesis: ἐκ … ἄραξε = ἐξήραξε; unaugmented; so the copies of Aristarchus and most others; Zenodotus read ἔαξε 'broke' (Merry's critical note on 12.422)
epic ποτί = πρός: 'close at the keel'

423.n: the stay from the masthead to the stern (Merry on 12.409); the verse opens with a short syllable, a στίχος ἀκέφαλος (Merry on 12.423); only here in Homer
unaugmented pluperfect passive (= ἐβέβλητο); Athenaeus, quoting the line, reads τετάνυστο (Merry on 12.423)
epic gen. -οιο; genitive of material with τετευχώς

423.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
423.n: the only perfect active of τεύχω with a passive sense; elsewhere τετυγμένος (Merry on 12.423)

424.n: dual, explained by τρόπιν ἠδὲ καὶ ἱστόν
unaugmented imperfect of συνεέργω (σύν + ἐέργω, epic for εἴργω): 'bind together', as 9.427

425.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

425.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); instrumental; ὀλοοῖς ἀνέμοισιν as 9.82

426.n: middle 'cease', with θύων; the half-line as 400

426.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

427.n: in tmesis: ἦλθε … ἐπί = ἐπῆλθε 'came on'

427.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
427.n: φέρων … θυμῷ is parenthetical: ὄφρα (428) follows directly on ἦλθε (Merry on 12.428)

428.n: = ὄφρα; purpose, with the optative after a past tense

428.g: I might measure out … the way to
428.n: 'measure back, retrace': = ἀναμετρήσας πέλαγος Χάρυβδιν ἱκοίμην, as πέλαγος μέγα μετρήσαντες 3.179 (Merry on 12.428); only here in Homer
the whirlpool under the fig tree (101–106); Apollonius the Sophist read θάλασσαν, which Nauck thinks right, though Plato (Epistle 7) and Plutarch quote Χάρυβδιν (Merry's critical note on 12.428)

429.n: unaugmented (= ἐφερόμην); the line after Iliad 1.592

429.p: verb · pres. part. act. dat. sg. masc.

430.n: 430–441 were doubted in many copies (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 12.430)

431.n: 'suck down, swallow' (ῥοῖβδος 'rushing noise'), as ἀναρροιβδεῖ 104; ρ doubled after the augment; the line after 236
'salt, briny'; in Homer only in the Odyssey, always with ὕδωρ

432.n: emphatic; the verb is ἐχόμην (433): 'but I, springing up toward a lofty fig tree, held on, clinging to it as a bat holds' (Merry on 12.432)
the wild fig tree above Charybdis (103)

432.p: verb · aor. part. pass. nom. sg. masc.

433.n: the fig tree; dative with προσφύς

433.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

434.n: intransitive here, 'plant myself firmly', where Iliad 21.242 has the middle στηρίξασθαι (Merry on 12.434)

435.n: 'far away', i.e. below; ἑκὰς εἶχον as ὑψόσʼ ἔχοντες 19.38 (Merry on 12.435)
intransitive, 'reached, stretched'; the scholia explain it as ὑπῆρχον 'were'; other copies have ἦσαν or ἔσσαν (Merry's critical note on 12.435)
'hanging aloft, out of reach' (cf. ἀείρω), with the long vowel seen in ἄωρτο; Bothe would write ἀπηόριοι (Merry on 12.435); only here in Homer

436.n: uncontracted (= κατεσκίων): 'overshadow'; only here in Homer

437.n: = ὄφρα; with the optative after a past tense: 'until she should'

438.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. sg. masc.
438.n: epic by-form ἐέλδομαι; agrees with μοι: 'they came to me as I longed'

439.n: = ὀψέ; 439–441 were objected to as contradicting the hours of the whirlpool: he reached Charybdis at sunrise (429), but the timbers came up only toward evening; and ἦμος δέ elsewhere in Homer always opens a verse (Merry on 12.439–441)
'when', answered by τῆμος (441); toward evening, when a judge has got through his cases and the market-place empties (Merry on 12.439–441)
ἀγορή 'assembly, market-place' with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word
intransitive root aorist; an aorist of custom (Merry on 12.439)

440.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
440.n: present where κρίνας might be expected, as ἐπαύσατο θύων 400, ἔγρετο εὕδων 13.187–188 (Merry on 12.439)

440.p: verb · pres. part. mid. gen. pl. masc.
440.n: middle 'go to law, plead one's case'

441.n: 'those timbers'; Aristarchus read τάδε (Merry's critical note on 12.441)
epic δοῦρα (= δόρατα): the mast and the keel
gen. -ιος; genitive of separation with ἐξ-
epic ἐξεφαάνθη (= ἐξεφάνθη); singular verb with neuter plural subject

442.n: κ-aorist of ἵημι 'let go'; not the adverb ἦκα 'softly'
the plural beside the dual χεῖρε: 'I let down hands and feet for a plunge' (Merry on 12.442)
infinitive of purpose, passive: 'so as to be carried down' (Merry on 12.442)

443.n: epic μέσσος = μέσος: in the middle (of the water) (Merry on 12.442)
'fall in with a thud' (δοῦπος): 'I plumped down', as ἄντλῳ δʼ ἐνδούπησε 15.479 (Merry on 12.442); in Homer only here and 15.479

444.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

444.n: 'row on, row across' (ἐρέσσω 'row'); in Homer only here and 14.351

445.n: subject of εἰσιδέειν (446), as the English takes it; since Scylla could not leave her rock, the scholia rejected 445–446, and Merry suggests ἐμέ as the subject: Zeus did not let him set eyes on Scylla again (Merry on 12.445–446 and his critical note)
Zeus; πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε as 1.28, Iliad 4.68

446.n: epic infinitive -έειν (= εἰσιδεῖν); the aorist εἰσεῖδον serves εἰσοράω
with the aorist indicative: what would have happened
'steep', i.e. utter; αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον as Iliad 6.57

447.n: agrees with νυκτί: dative of time

448.n: νῆσον ἐς Ὠγυγίην as 1.85; the line = 7.254
Ionic ἐς = εἰς, placed after its noun

449.n: θεός of a goddess; δεινὴ θεὸς αὐδήεσσα as 11.8, of Circe

450.n: adverbial 'why?': here Odysseus turns and addresses Alcinous directly (Merry on 12.450)
'tell over a tale' (μῦθος + λέγω); in Homer only here and 453

451.n: 'already': ἤδη … χθιζός 'already yesterday', i.e. only yesterday
adjective where English uses an adverb: the tale of Ogygia told the evening before, 7.244 ff. (Merry on 12.451 refers to his note on 7.244)

452.n: accented before enclitic τε; resumes τοι (451)

453.n: epic αὖτις = αὖθις; join αὖτις with μυθολογεύειν and ἀριζήλως with εἰρημένα (Merry on 12.453)
